rules.sentence: A high level of suspicion is still necessary for the diagnosis of GALD-NH.

Characteristic facial features, bile duct paucity, chronic cholestasis, and anomalies in the skeletal (butterfly vertebrae), ocular (posterior embryotoxon), renal, vascular, and cardiac (pulmonary stenosis) systems are among the syndrome’s clinical characteristics.
Cholestasis typically manifests within the first year of life, and many newborns are assessed for conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and scleral icterus within the first few weeks of their birth.

During this time, coagulopathy is probably caused by a fat-soluble vitamin deficiency from severe cholestasis, which results in a vitamin K deficiency that can be readily corrected with supplementation.
According to reports, only 20–30% of patients with ALGS require a liver transplant, making the hepatic prognosis previously thought to be favorable.
